sections.text:
In a forest ruled by the law of power, there lived a nervous lion who hated any animal that had long, sharp horns, because he was jealous of them and they reminded him of strong competitors.

The angry lion issued a strict royal decree: “Any animal with horns on its head shall be expelled from my forest immediately! Whoever is caught will be devoured!”

Panic spread among the horned animals such as deer, antelope, and wild bulls, and they began to pack their belongings to escape from the forest as quickly as possible.

There was a small rabbit with very long, pointed ears, living peacefully in his burrow.

When the little rabbit heard this decree, he was extremely terrified and began to tremble. He immediately began gathering his food and belongings to leave the forest with the fleeing animals!
His neighbor, the squirrel, saw him in amazement and asked him: “Where are you going, my rabbit friend? You are not one of those with horns! The lion only expelled those with horns, not those with ears!”

The rabbit answered as he gasped in fear and looked right and left: “I know that, my neighbor! But what if the nervous lion looked at my long, erect ears and said that they were horns and not ears?!”

The squirrel laughed and said, "That's stupid! Anyone can tell the difference between an ear and a horn!"

The rabbit replied with wisdom mixed with fear: “When a tyrannical and stupid person has absolute power, he does not listen to logic or reason! If he decides that my ears are horns, who will dare to oppose him or prove the opposite? He will eat me before I can explain the difference to him!”

The rabbit carried his bag and ran out of the forest, leaving behind a very important lesson; It is that living under an unjust and tyrannical rule that does not recognize logic is a constant danger, and that it is better and safer to stay away from a place that is not governed by reason or justice in order to protect your life from false accusations and absolute capriciousness.
